pushed.name: Chalk and Corner
pushed.description: Four corner stones. Each one has a chalk mark. Record what is on each stone and the hour you saw it. Do not scrub anything. Do not add anything.
pushed.successDescription: The chalk marks were a schedule, not a boundary.

objectives.description:
The mission desk is busy. The handler does not look up. He slides a folded paper across and keeps talking to someone else.

The slip reads: C rank. Survey. Four corner stones.

Inside are four rubbings: chalk marks pressed onto paper with the flat side of a pencil. One mark from each stone.

The job: record what is on each stone, and the hour you saw it. Do not scrub anything. Do not add anything.

Someone has added a note at the bottom in different handwriting: best guess is territory. Four marks, four owners.

nextObjectiveId.text: Four gangs would mean four fights.

objectives.description:
But nobody has been hurt on any of those four streets. Not once.

So the marks are not a war over territory. They are something else.

The stone worth watching is the one that changes.
Four corners, an hour of walking between them, and one afternoon.

nextObjectiveId.text: Walk all four and record them.

objectives.description: You spend an hour on the tannery row asking who chalks the corner stones.

Nobody chalks the corner stones. Nobody has even seen it happen. Two people ask if you are from the cartage office.

An hour spent, and you learned one thing: someone has asked this street these same questions before.
The first corner is exactly where the rubbing says. So is the second.

The third stone has two strokes instead of one. The second stroke is new, still powdery at the edge where nobody has stepped on it.

The fourth stone has one stroke, older than the rest.

Four corners, four hours, and one stone that changed today.

nextObjectiveId.text: Wait by the third stone and watch who comes.
Hand in the survey and let the office work it out.

objectives.description: You pick a doorway across from the third stone. You settle in and watch.

Someone comes. They crouch at the stone with a chalk stub and start a third stroke. They do not look around once.

They keep glancing up at the light, not at the street. They are checking the hour.

They place the new stroke beside the old one, with the same gap between.
Rag over the mouth. No plate on the forehead. They grab for the chalk first, not for you. The chalk matters more to them than the fight.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They wipe out the half-made stroke with a sleeve and go over the wall before you are on your feet.

By the time you are up, the lane is empty again. Somewhere out of sight, a stroke is going onto another stone.

You hand in the four rubbings, the four hours, and what you saw in the alley.

The handler reads your notes once in the order you walked them. Then again in the order the strokes were made. Then he looks up.

"These are not property marks. Each stroke is an hour. The stones are a schedule. Someone is telling someone else when a lane will be empty."

"Not four owners. A queue."

"These crews do not know each other, and they do not want to. Two of them working the same lane on the same night is how people get seen. But you cannot sort that out in a room, because a room means faces, and a face is the one thing none of them will give up."

"So they sort it out on a wall. Nobody meets anybody, and everybody knows whose hour it is."

You hand in the four rubbings and the four hours. That is the job, all of it.

The handler checks them off, pays out, and drops them in a tray with forty other surveys.

Someone will read them properly in a month.

nextObjectiveId.text: That is the job, all of it.

objectives.description: Survey filed.
Four corners, and one stone that changed.

pushed.name: The Empty Contract
pushed.description: A dead courier was carrying a strange contract. It names a place, a night, and a price, but it does not say what the job is. The price is far too high for a simple beating. The night is tonight.
pushed.successDescription: Nobody was planning a robbery. Someone was paid to time the patrols, and that number will sell to anybody.

objectives.description:
The handler has a paper under a stone and a mission slip clipped to it.

The slip reads: C rank. The paper was taken off a courier found dead on the north road. It looked like an accident. There was nothing else on the body.

nextObjectiveId.text: Just tell me where to be.

objectives.description:
Four lines. A place. A night. A price. Instead of a signature, only a drawn mark.

There is no instruction of any kind. And the price is enough money to live on for a season.

nextObjectiveId.text: Too much money for a simple job.

objectives.description:
That much money does not buy a beating. It buys something else.

And the paper never says what. A place, a night, a price, and no task written anywhere on it.

Which is the point. A contract that names the job can only be carried by somebody allowed to know the job. This one can be dropped in a road.

The place is the roof of a disused dyer's shop on the tannery row. The building is empty. The yard behind it is empty. Nothing there is worth stealing.

So the roof itself is not the prize. The prize is what you can see from the roof.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go and look at what the roof can see.

objectives.description:
The dyer's shop is four storeys of empty building on a corner nobody uses.

The roof looks straight down onto the north watch post, and onto both streets the night patrol uses.

Someone is lying flat at the roof edge, chin on their arms. They have been up there for hours. Every few minutes they scratch a mark into a wax tablet without taking their eyes off the street.

nextObjectiveId.text: Climb the back wall. Slow, but silent.
Take the stairs. Fast, but loud.
Wait at the bottom door. They must come down.

objectives.description: The back wall is brick under forty years of ivy. Climbing it quietly takes a long time. Quiet is the whole point.

You come over the roof edge eight feet behind them. They do not hear you.

The tablet lies open beside their elbow, and they are still writing. Four hours of marks, and every mark is neat and steady.
You wait by the alley door at the bottom of the stairs. Everyone has to come down eventually.

They come down four hours later, at the end of their shift, and walk straight past you. To them, you are just someone waiting in a doorway.

The tablet is inside their coat.
They only notice the danger when you are four feet away. They grab for the tablet, not for a weapon.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They get over the far wall with the tablet and are gone into the tannery row.

But the contract pays for a full night of times, and half a tablet is worth nothing. Before long, a figure climbs back onto the roof and settles in again.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go back to the dyer's roof.

objectives.description:
The stair door is stiff, and it screeches loud enough to warn the whole building. By the time you reach the roof, they are already two roofs away with the tablet under one arm.

You chase them over four roofs, a yard wall, and half the tannery row.
You corner them in a dead end above the drying sheds. Even now, they try to slip past you instead of fighting you.

objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They jump off the drying shed roof into the dark and take the tablet with them.

But the contract pays for a full night of times, and half a tablet is worth nothing. Before long, they are back at the roof edge, writing again.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go back to the dyer's roof.

objectives.description:
The watcher sits against the wall, beaten, and says nothing. They watch you read.

Four hours of times and nothing else. Two columns, one for each patrol street. A mark every time the patrol comes out. A mark every time it goes back in.

At the bottom, underlined twice, a single number: eleven.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the tablet back to the hall.

At the hall, the handler reads halfway down the second column and goes quiet. He reads it again from the top.

"Look at the handwriting. Steady all the way through. Four hours of marks, and it never shook once."

"A thief planning his own robbery would be nervous. This is a copyist's hand. Someone paid to write down times, and never told them what the times were for."

"And here is what they proved. Twice a night, for eleven minutes, nobody is watching the north post. That gap is the product. A number like that will sell to anybody."

He puts the tablet down on top of the contract.

"The courier was not killed, by the way. He came off a wet road in the dark and broke his neck on it. Nobody arranged that."

"Everything these people build is designed so that no one person knows enough to give the rest away. It works. And then it rains."

pushed.name: Nothing to Report
pushed.description: A warehouse clerk is carrying two years of bonded collection sheets to a village audit that sits at first light. The people who would rather those books did not arrive are trained. Safehouse to records hall, before dawn.
pushed.successDescription: The books went onto the audit table at first light. They name a broker, a bank and eleven dates, and not one member of the Forsworn, because the clerk has never met one.

objectives.description:
B rank. An escort. One clerk, one satchel, safehouse to records hall, before dawn.

The desk sends this one upstairs.

"Warehouse clerk. He is carrying two years of collection sheets from the bonded yard on the canal, and the audit opens at first light."

"B rank, because I expect the people who would rather those books did not arrive to be trained."

nextObjectiveId.text: Does anybody know he came to us?

objectives.description:
"Somebody does. He has not been at work in two days, and nobody from that office has asked why. An office that does not ask is an office that has been told not to."

"They do not need him dead. They need him not to arrive, and that can be bought on a road or bought at a door."

"Assume both have been bought, and assume the two were bought separately. Nothing these people do is organised from one desk. That is the only reason any of it is survivable."

The clerk is in the front room with his coat already on and the satchel in his lap.

"I am not brave. I want that written somewhere."

"I countersigned eleven of these. I would like the audit to be able to say that I stopped at eleven."

The clerk waits in the front room with his coat on and the satchel held in both hands. He does not ask where you are taking him. He is saving his questions.

Four ways out of the district, and first light is coming.
The north gate is shut at this hour, which you knew. The wall beside it is not.

You are up the wall and back down inside a minute. Then you look at a man of fifty holding a satchel with both hands.

He does not say anything. He does not have to.
You take the market row at his pace and hang back a little, listening for anyone who takes note of him.

Three lit corners and perhaps sixty people, and nobody stops you.

At the second corner, a figure sitting on a barrel looks at the clerk's face slightly too long, then looks down again, and does not move.

"That man knows me. He signs for the cartage at the yard."

He says it without stopping. Somebody is going to know which way you went, and the night gives them time to be somewhere before you are.
The lanes are shorter and unlit, and unlit lanes in this district have owners. You read the corner stone before you take the third turn.

One chalk stroke, low, and the powder at its edge is fresh.

Somebody has claimed this lane for an hour tonight. And you are about to walk a man of fifty down it.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go anyway. Better here than at the hall.

objectives.description:
They come off the wall at the halfway point, quick and light and not interested in you at all. They go past your shoulder, for the man behind you.

Not a robbery. Not a warning. Somebody was told a lane, an hour, and a face.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
You are turned around for two seconds, and the lane is empty behind you.

Two streets over you find him against a wall, with the satchel in both hands and no intention of letting go of it.

"I did not run. I want that written down as well."

nextObjectiveId.text: Back to the safehouse and start again.

objectives.description: The towpath is long and wet and empty, and there is a patrol on it that you have to wait out before you can put a civilian on the bank.

Fifty minutes gone that you did not have.

The clerk does not complain once. Somewhere behind the roofline, the sky stops being black and starts being a colour.

You are going to arrive. You are going to arrive in daylight. And anyone who wanted time to get ahead of you has had it.
You bring him up the last four streets slowly, stop him at the corner, and give the hall steps a long look.

One of them. Blank half mask, hands where you can see them, making no attempt at all to hide. They have been sitting there a long time.

The clerk makes a small sound.

nextObjectiveId.text: Tell him the truth about what happens after.
Tell him it ends when the books are on the table.

objectives.description:
You tell him the truth. Handing those books over makes him a witness. A witness is a thing with a price on it. The village will move him, and being moved is not the same as being safe.

He listens to all of it.

"Eleven."

He walks past you toward the steps, and he does not look at the wall.

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will handle the wall.

objectives.description:
You tell him it ends when the books are on the table. That he goes home afterwards. That the wall is nothing he needs to think about.

He believes you, which is worse than if he had not.

He goes up the steps almost quickly, and the relief on his face is going to be a thing you remember.

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will handle the wall.

objectives.description:
They stand up only when the hall door closes behind him. They were never here for the clerk. They were here for you.

Think it through and it is simple. If the one who walked him gets home untouched, the next clerk finds an escort willing too. They were paid to make sure the next clerk does not.

No talking. No offer. No attempt to leave.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They were waiting a long time, and they are not tired.

They leave you where you fall. The beating was the message, and it has been delivered.

When you get up, the wall opposite is empty, and the clerk is inside with four hours of auditors and no idea that any of it happened.

The books go onto the audit table at first light, and the auditors have four hours with them before anyone else is awake.

A broker, a bank, eleven dates, and a delay column nobody outside the yard has ever seen.

Not one line of it names a Forsworn. It never could. The clerk has never met one. That was always the point of the crates.

She reads the auditors' first note standing up.

"That is a case. Cases against these people are thin on the ground."

Then she asks what you told him on the steps. Flatly, the way she asks things she has already guessed.

nextObjectiveId.text: I told him it ends when the books land.

objectives.description:
She nods once, and does not look relieved.

"Good. He handed them over knowing, which means the audit has a witness who understood what he was doing. That holds up in court."

"Also, he deserved to know. I would put that reason first. But on a bad night you will only have one of the two, and either will do."

She puts the note down and looks at you slightly too long.

"He will find out. Not tonight, and not from me. And he will remember that somebody stood on those steps and told him otherwise."

She does not raise her voice at any point.

"The audit stands. Next time, tell them, and let them be brave on purpose. It holds up better in court, and it holds up better afterwards."
Clerk delivered.
The safehouse, and four ways out of the district.

Your eyes wander the board, sorting by rank. Then you see it.

An old Bingo Book entry, faded and worn, pinned to the board with a fresh mission brief.

Dangerous and resourceful fugitive from justice. Old Ghost once ran an ANBU cell in this village.

Current whereabouts unknown. Slums district is a good lead.

If he really is back, time matters. Someone like that moving freely inside the walls will not stay quiet for long.

You think about where to begin.
The wall walk runs the whole northern span. If he came in, he came over something.

Nothing. Fresh mortar, a bored sentry, and a long climb for no reason.

The sentry has been on this stretch eleven days and has seen nobody but the mortar crew.

You are looking in the wrong place.
The market is loud, crowded, and full of people who would notice a stranger. You work the stalls.

A courier. Fourteen years old, terrified, carrying somebody's laundry.

You send him on and lean against the wall.

Time you do not have.

The room is small and he keeps his voice down the whole time.

"Old Ghost. Yes. Warehouse off the cut, tonight."

He gives you a door and does not ask why you want it.

This was never his location.

You come to on an empty floor with two hours gone and a door standing open.

Two down in an empty building. Nobody here has been in the same district as Old Ghost tonight.

A setup. Not by your contact, who was told the same thing you were, but by whoever fed it to him.

Somebody wanted you in an empty warehouse for two hours.

Two of them are not his.

They are good. Spaced, quiet, and taking the route with the fewest windows on it. You follow anyway.

At the third corner the lead figure stops without turning around.

They know.
The two at the back turn to meet you and the third does not. He is already moving, and he does not look back once.

The house at the bottom of the slope is empty by the time you get down to it.

Two down in the lane, and a long way up the slope somebody is still running.

He has not looked back once, which means he knew the other two were staying the moment he decided to leave them.
You go after him. Over the slope, across four roofs, down into the drainage cut and out the other side.

He runs out of village before he runs out of breath.

The cut ends at the wall and he turns to face you, and he is not even breathing hard.

"You are the fifth," he says. "Or the sixth. I have stopped counting properly."
No escort, no rafters, and nowhere left to be. He rolls his shoulder once and waits for you to come to him.

Alone at the foot of the wall, with the two he left behind still in a lane on the other side of the slope.

You file it that night. Old Ghost. Bingo Book entry. Taken inside the village.

She reads it. Then reads it again.

"I believe your report. I have believed four of them."

She signs it and does not close the entry.

"Because he taught me how to be sure."

"That is all you get. The entry stays open. It always does."

objectives.description:
He is over the verge and into the treeline, and you have nothing but a day of walking.

Somewhere behind you a doss house is pointing somebody at a scrap yard.
You still know people from before you made rank. One of them runs a back room off the tannery row and owes you nothing, which is why he will talk.

The room is small and he keeps his voice down the whole time.

"Old Ghost. Yes. Warehouse off the cut, tonight."

He gives you a door and does not ask why you want it.

The door is unlocked, the warehouse is empty, and two come off the rafters the moment you are three steps in.

This was never his location.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The rafters were a good place to wait and they had been waiting a while.

You come to on an empty floor with two hours gone and a door standing open.

Two down in an empty building. Nobody here has been in the same district as Old Ghost tonight.

A setup. Not by your contact, who was told the same thing you were, but by whoever fed it to him.

Somebody wanted you in an empty warehouse for two hours.

nextObjectiveId.text: So where were they not sending me?

objectives.description: You go back to what you were told and work out what it was built to keep you away from. The cut runs north to the old dye works and the dye works have a night watchman nobody has paid in a month.

The dye works. Two hours late, but not too late.

There are lights on in a building that has no reason to have lights, and three sets of prints in the yard mud.

Two of them are not his.
He does not look surprised to see you. The other two move to put you between them, and he lets them, and only then does he step forward himself.

objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Three of them in a yard, and the two were only ever there to hold you still.

By the time you are up the dye works are dark and the lights are off in a building that had no reason to have them.
You find a roofline with a view of the whole eastern quarter and you wait for the light to go.
Two hours after dusk, three figures leave a house at the bottom of the slope and move up the lane without lamps.

They are good. Spaced, quiet, and taking the route with the fewest windows on it. You follow anyway.

At the third corner the lead figure stops without turning around.

They know.
The two at the back turn to meet you and the third does not. He is already moving, and he does not look back once.

objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
Two of them in a narrow lane is a poor place to be, and the third is gone regardless.

The house at the bottom of the slope is empty by the time you get down to it.

Two down in the lane, and a long way up the slope somebody is still running.

He has not looked back once, which means he knew the other two were staying the moment he decided to leave them.
You go after him. Over the slope, across four roofs, down into the drainage cut and out the other side.

He runs out of village before he runs out of breath.

The cut ends at the wall and he turns to face you, and he is not even breathing hard.

"You are the fifth," he says. "Or the sixth. I have stopped counting properly."
No escort, no rafters, and nowhere left to be. He rolls his shoulder once and waits for you to come to him.

objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
He has been getting out of places like this since before you were born.

When you look up, the foot of the wall is empty and there is nothing to say he was ever standing at it.

Alone at the foot of the wall, with the two he left behind still in a lane on the other side of the slope.

Three down in a dye works yard. He waited for the other two to commit before he moved once, which is how he has stayed in that Bingo Book.

He is down at the verge with his business already concluded and nothing on him to show what it was.

You file it that night. Old Ghost. Bingo Book entry. Taken inside the village.

She reads it. Then reads it again.

"...Did you?"

"I believe your report. I have believed four of them."

She signs it and does not close the entry.

"He was ANBU here once. I was on the road the first time somebody confirmed him dead. Take the pay and do not think about it too hard."

nextObjectiveId.text: Ask how she was so sure it was him.

objectives.description:
She signs it without another word and does not close the entry.

When you are at the door she says it to your back.

"Many have reported the same. Myself included."

"Because he taught me how to be sure."

She does not look up from the page.

"That is all you get. The entry stays open. It always does."

nextObjectiveId.text: The entry stays open. It always does.

objectives.description:
The pay is A rank and it clears the same day.

The entry stays open.
Report filed. Entry open.
The slums, and three ways to work it.
The board, and four places to look.

pushed.name: The Tenth Name
pushed.description: A page taken off a body lists ten entries. Nine are copied out of our own Bingo Book in a hand that is not ours. The tenth has no name on it, only a service number with this village's prefix and a date eight months out. Copies are in transit.
pushed.successDescription: Nobody infiltrated anything. The four fields on every entry are public record, printed by this village about its own people and pinned to a wall.

objectives.description: A rank. Retrieval. The briefing room, and a single page on the table, folded twice.

Ten entries.

"Nine of them I recognise, because nine of them are entries out of our own Bingo Book, copied in a hand that is not ours."

"They keep a book on themselves. On its own that is a week's work."

The tenth line has no name on it. A service number, a village prefix, and a date eight months out.

The prefix is ours.

"Currently serving, with a date on them like a delivery."

She does not look the number up in front of you.

nextObjectiveId.text: What do you want me to bring back?

objectives.description:
"This page is stock. Copies are moving between their people right now, and every hour it circulates it goes somewhere I cannot follow."

"Take one out of transit and bring me the route it was on. Page and route. Not the person."

Three places a copy might be moving through, and one of them is a cold room.
You walk the canal frontage looking for a stone with two strokes on it.

Four stones, four single strokes, none of them fresh.

The lanes here were worked last week and have not been booked since. Whatever is moving is not moving through this frontage tonight.
The gate ledgers go back a month and every line of them is somebody's name.

Nobody carrying that page walked through a gate and signed for it.

An afternoon proving that people who deal in unsigned paper also do not sign for themselves.
The body it came off is still in the cold room, unidentified, which is the normal outcome and not a failure. You go through the coat seam by seam.

No plate, no papers. In the coat lining, a chalk stub worn to the length of a thumbnail.

The page was carried folded twice against the body, the way you carry something you refer to often.

Working stock, not a delivery. Which means a route, and a route means a runner.
Three ways to take a copy out of transit, and only one night to do it.

nextObjectiveId.text: Stand in the lane at the hour and take it.
Follow a runner instead of stopping one.

objectives.description: You take the third street of the frontage, where the stone has two strokes and the second is still powdery, and you give it the hour.

Two come down the lane at the hour the chalk gives. They stop when they see somebody standing in it.

There is a pause in which one of them clearly considers explaining that you are in the wrong place, and then decides against it.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The lane empties in both directions and takes the hour with it.

In the morning the stone has been scrubbed and there are three fresh strokes on a corner two streets over.
You pick up a runner at the frontage and stay with them for four streets without closing, which is harder than closing.
You stay with the chain for two hours and write down every stone it touches.

Four handovers in two hours, none of them the same person twice, every one at a corner stone.

Nobody passes a page. They pass a place.

The route runs inward from the canal and ends at a reading room off the records annexe.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the last one in the chain.

objectives.description: The last runner in the chain is standing in the annexe doorway with a copy in their hand and no idea that the four ahead of them are already accounted for.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
They are through the annexe door and into the boards room before you are past the step, and out the other side into a street full of people.

The chain will not run that route again this week.
You spend the evening in the wrong sort of room asking what a copy of a page would cost.

It costs about what a good meal costs, which is the single most useful thing you learn all night.

The man who sells it has never read it, cannot read most of it, and does not care. He copies what he is given and sells the copies on.

"They are not secret," he says, honestly baffled by the question. "They are just not for you."

nextObjectiveId.text: Buy one and ask where his came from.

objectives.description: He tells you, and then the two men whose route you have just bought your way into come through the door behind you.

objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: You go out of the window and the room is empty behind you, and by morning nobody in that quarter is selling anything to anybody.

The nine known entries all carry the same three fields under the name. A year, a prefix, and a single word.

Passed. Debt. Discipline. Passed. Clanless. Debt. Discipline. Passed. Debt.
You take the reading room itself and go through what is pinned up in it.

Promotion boards go up on a wall four times a year. The lending register is open to any creditor who asks. Discipline dockets are posted so the punishment is seen to be done.

Nobody infiltrated anything.

This village publishes a list of the people it has disappointed, on purpose, and somebody has been walking in and reading it.

She reads the four fields before she reads the tenth line.

"Every one of these is on a wall somewhere in this village with my authority at the bottom of it."

"They are not recruiting out of our ranks. They are standing at the bottom of a slope we built and pointed downhill."

nextObjectiveId.text: Eight months is a forecast, not a plan.
The tenth has not done anything.

objectives.description:
"A forecast that will probably be right, which is worse. Nobody has spoken to this person. Nobody has offered them anything."

"Somebody read four public facts and wrote a date, and on the evidence of the nine above it I would not bet against the date."

nextObjectiveId.text: So what happens to the page?

objectives.description:
"Nothing at all. Which is the problem I am about to have upstairs, because the moment this goes up, everybody matching those four fields becomes a watch list."

"And then the date will be right for reasons we caused."

nextObjectiveId.text: So what happens to the page?

objectives.description:
She has the page and the route, which is what she asked for. What happens next is not a field decision, and she says so, and then asks anyway.

"You walked that route. Tell me what you think and then I will ignore you if I want to."

nextObjectiveId.text: Put the page up and let us read it too.

objectives.description:
Somebody knocks. Not you, and not that week.

It comes back as a line in a personnel note. The officer was spoken to, was cooperative, and has requested no further contact.

"Cooperative," she reads out, with no expression at all.

"They now know they were on a list. The date is still eight months away and I have made it more likely, not less."

She files the page.

"The page was worth taking. What we do with it is a different problem and it is mine."

Nobody knocks. The service number is never looked up.

What goes upstairs is a proposal about the reading room, and it takes seven months and most of her remaining goodwill.

It removes exactly one of the four fields.

"One of four means the next list is harder to build and less accurate. It is also the only one of the four that cost this village nothing to give up, which is why it is the one I got."

"Be angrier about that than I am able to be in this office."

The page goes up with your report and the route drawn out in full.

It comes back in nine days approved for circulation to section heads. Everybody matching those four fields is now a name on a desk somewhere.

"They wanted it read. Now it is read by us as well, and I cannot decide whether that is counter-intelligence or doing their filing."

She signs the circulation.

"Nine of those section heads will treat it as a warning about the village. One will treat it as a list of suspects. I do not get to choose which."
Page recovered.
The frontage, and the chain of runners.
The page, and what is on it.
